newsitem.title: LATVIA: CENTRAL BANK TO BOOST CAPITAL TO 25 MLN LATS.
newsitem.headline: CENTRAL BANK TO BOOST CAPITAL TO 25 MLN LATS.

text.p: The board of the Bank of Latvia said on Wednesday that the government's economy committee had approved changes to the central bank law which will allow it to boost its capital to 25 million lats from 2.5 million lats.
The amendments must still be approved by the government and parliament.

"One reason for doing this is to be able, if the need arises, to protect the stability of the national currency in the future," Ilmar Rimshevics, the deputy president of the central bank, told a news conferemce.
Rimshevics said that the Bank of Latvia had the lowest levels of capital among the three central banks in the Baltic countries.
"Estonia and Lithuania's central banks have capital in the range of 60 to 70 million lats," Rimshevics said.
"Our initial capital of 500 million roubles is outdated both morally and physically," he added.
